archetype.name: Dual-Threat (pocket-leaning)
archetype.definition: A quarterback who has always paired a downfield arm with real running value, now leaning more on the pocket as his designed-run game has stalled and his scrambles carry most of his rushing value.

report.headline: Downfield throws still land; the easy throws are the problem in Philadelphia.
report.take:
Hurts has spent his prime as an efficient dual-threat starter. His 2022 EPA per play ranked 5th, his 2024 CPOE ranked 1st, and he has ranked top six in QB rushing yards every full season. This year looks nothing like that so far. His -0.058 passing EPA per dropback ranks 31st of 45, his CPOE has fallen 5.7 points from last season to -2.55, and PFR charts 21.4% of his throws as bad, 37th of 38 and well above the 14.3% he posted last year. That bad-throw rate is close to his rookie 24.3%, not anything from his peak years.

The odd part is where the damage sits. On throws of 10+ air yards he has been excellent: +0.878 EPA per attempt, a +8.7 CPOE, and six of his eight touchdowns. The intermediate window (+0.922, 62% success) has been his best area. Everything under 10 yards has fallen apart: -0.352 EPA per attempt, a -7.1 CPOE, and -38 EPA added up, which more than cancels the deep work. Throws behind the line have gone 9% successful. Under-center dropbacks show a -20 CPOE. So this is not a quarterback who has lost his arm or his nerve. Screens, checkdowns and timing throws are breaking down. That points to a mix of misfires, poor blocking on screens, and a thin set of targets (only Dontayvion Wicks, Darius Cooper and Dallas Goedert have been clearly positive per target). His aggressiveness has also dipped to 14.3% from 17.8%, so he is throwing into fewer tight windows and still missing the open ones.

The numbers flatter him in places too. The 5.2% TD rate ranks 15th, propped up by a red-zone line of 5 TDs on 14 plays. He has zero fumbles lost despite three turnover-worthy fumbles. Both are luck that tends to even out. Meanwhile the trend is bad. In Weeks 3-5 the Eagles went 0-3 and he posted -0.199 EPA per dropback with a -9.9 CPOE. Week 4 against the Rams (93 yards, 36% bad throws) was the low point. He then missed Week 6, which Tanner McKee started. He returned as the Week 7 starter, but that game isn't in this log, so his post-injury form is an open question.

The rushing side is shrinking as well. He is at 21.4 yards a game against 26.3 last year, continuing a slide from the 700-plus-yard seasons. Designed runs have been stuffed 55.6% of the time at 1.11 a carry. His scrambles (+0.33 EPA each, 5 first downs on 12) are now the useful part of his legs. The ceiling games still come from the deep ball, but the floor depends on fixing the short game, and the supporting cast is going the wrong way for that.

strengths.title: Intermediate and deep accuracy intact
strengths.body: On 10+ air-yard throws he is +0.878 EPA per attempt with a +8.7 CPOE, and the 10-19 range is his best area by far. That matches the career profile of an accurate downfield passer. Because it is skill rather than scheme luck, it should hold. The risk is volume, since his aggressiveness is down and he is not testing these windows as often as last year.

strengths.title: Scrambles still buy yards
strengths.body: When the pocket breaks down he still makes it pay, at +0.33 EPA per scramble with 5 first downs on 12. That is the trade that justifies his 3.04-second time to throw. His 27.1% pressure-to-sack rate sits mid-pack and is better than several of his past seasons. The legs as a planned weapon are fading, but the improvising version still works.

strengths.title: Red-zone finishing
strengths.body: Five touchdowns on 14 red-zone plays with a +14.8 CPOE keep his TD rate at 5.2%, 15th in the league, even with poor overall efficiency. His red-zone value is real, combining his legs and an accurate short-area finish. A rate this high on so few plays will cool, though.

concerns.title: The short game has collapsed
concerns.body: Throws under 10 air yards have produced -38 EPA, and passes behind the line are 9% successful. That single bucket explains his entire negative season. It reflects missed easy throws (a 21.4% bad-throw rate) plus screens that go nowhere behind a patched line. Because it clashes with six years of accurate short passing, some bounce-back is likely. Until his health and his line settle, though, it is the main drag.

concerns.title: Sliding into and out of injury
concerns.body: Before missing Week 6 he went 0-3 with -0.199 EPA per dropback and a -9.9 CPOE. A cause, possibly whatever kept him out, is more plausible than a sudden loss of skill. His CPOE is down 5.7 points from last year. The data shows nothing about how he looked in his Week 7 return, so the rebound is an assumption, not a finding.

concerns.title: Thin cast, missing right tackle
concerns.body: Lane Johnson is out with an estimated return after the season. Wicks, his most productive target at +19.9 EPA, and DeVonta Smith were both inactive for the Week 7 Monday game against Dallas. A sack rate ranked 31st and a 16.8% hit-or-sacked rate already show a leaky pocket. Losing the right tackle and the best route-runner makes the timing game harder to repair.

trend.note: Two efficient-enough wins opened the season, then three straight losses dragged his EPA per dropback to -0.199, bottoming out at 93 yards against the Rams. He missed Week 6 and returned in Week 7, a game not in this log.

nextGame.headline: A soft Washington secondary he already beat once
nextGame.body:
Washington's defense ranks 25th in EPA and 26th against the pass, and it allows 22.2 PPR a game to quarterbacks (30th). Offenses throw on it more than anywhere else in the league: its pass rate over norm ranks 1st. The fit with Hurts's profile is close to perfect. Their deep defense ranks 22nd, which suits his best area. Their short defense ranks 7th, which is the exact zone where he has been bleeding EPA. Their 25th-ranked sack rate gives him time to hold the ball and find the intermediate window. In Week 1 against this team he threw 3 TDs, ran for 46 yards and had his best fantasy day.

The Book has Philadelphia as a 4.5-point road underdog with a 40.5 total, a lean toward a trailing, pass-heavy script. Availability is the swing. Wicks and Smith carry estimated return dates of this game, but both were inactive last week. Johnson is out, and Saquon Barkley is questionable after a hamstring-and-back game, which affects the run threat behind his designed keepers. On Washington's side, DT Javon Kinlaw and DE Charles Omenihu are both questionable, which could thin an already modest rush. Terry McLaurin is out and Marcus Mariota is questionable, which could cap Washington's scoring and keep the game close. The early forecast shows gusts in the mid-20s, worth checking closer to kickoff for the deep game.

keyMatchups.title: His deep ball vs their deep defense
keyMatchups.body: Washington allows +0.689 EPA on deep throws, 22nd in the league, while Hurts is +0.802 on 20+ air yards. This is where a big game would come from. It depends on whether he has Wicks or Smith to throw to.

keyMatchups.title: Goedert against a leaky TE defense
keyMatchups.body: Top tight ends have scored 9.1 PPR over their averages against Washington, the worst mark in the league. Goedert has been +0.454 EPA per target. With the receiver room uncertain, he is the most reliable route to the middle of the field, where Hurts has 3 TDs.

keyMatchups.title: Short game into a strong short defense
keyMatchups.body: Washington's short-pass defense ranks 7th, and his under-10 throws are -0.352 EPA per attempt. If the offense keeps feeding screens and quick throws, the drives will die there again.

nextGame.watch: Whether Wicks and Smith are active. With them, the deep-shot plan against Washington's weak back end works; without them, he is leaning on Goedert and the broken short game.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect a passer somewhere between his slump and his career norm. A quarterback with a +7.5 CPOE two seasons ago and bad-throw rates in the 12-14% range every year since his rookie season is unlikely to stay at 21.4% if he is healthy. The intermediate and deep efficiency is the real part of his game. The short-game numbers should drift back toward average simply because they are so far outside his history. Working against that, the line has lost Lane Johnson for the year and the target pool behind Wicks and Goedert has been weak. That caps the recovery at roughly league-average efficiency rather than his 2022-24 level.

The TD rate and the zero lost fumbles are the parts likely to regress. His rushing should settle around 15-28 yards a game, carried by scrambles more than designed runs. That keeps a fantasy floor of about 12 points while the ceiling depends on deep shots landing. A 2-3 team with a 27th-ranked defense should be throwing plenty, which supports his volume even if efficiency stays middling.

confidence.note: Five-game sample, an unexplained missed start, a Week 7 return not in the log, and key teammates' availability unsettled.
